role: FitnessPostSummaryView extension: the 'How did that feel?' rating (save to archive), the legacy analysis-snapshot backfill, the 'How you did' narrative (snapshot or legacy on-the-fly sentences), hero card inputs, recover/retrim controls, partial-data banner, key-stat tiles, α1 band helpers for the hero, and the static route map.
types: FitnessPostSummaryView: extension — feeling, snapshot backfill, narratives, hero, key stats, map
FitnessPostSummaryView.PartialBannerChrome: struct (ViewModifier) — orange rounded background/border for the partial-data banner
toplevel: File-scope private func hrrSentence (line 661). No globals.

flags.text: File header says the hero, HRR banner and key-stats grid live in FitnessPostSummaryView.swift, but heroCard and keyStatsCard are declared in this file and the HRR banner is in WorkoutStatsCards.

sessionAnalysisCard doc says the narrative includes 'TRIMP relative to the user's typical load', but trimpSentence uses fixed 150/80/30 Lucia TRIMP bands with no per-user comparison (its own comment admits this).

units.does: Shows the WorkoutFeelingBadge when a rating is stored and not editing, otherwise the WorkoutFeelingPrompt. Rendered twice (top and footer) sharing feelingEditing.

branches.cond: stored workoutFeeling non-nil AND feelingEditing false
branches.effect: true: badge; false: prompt (unrated or editing)

units.does: WorkoutFeelingPrompt pre-filled with the stored rating/note; select spawns saveWorkoutFeeling, skip calls skipFeeling.
units.entry: Rendered from feelingSection; onSelect/onSkip closures fire on user taps.

units.does: Sets feelingEditing = false (leaves an unrated session unrated, or cancels editing).
WorkoutFeelingBadge showing rating and note; tap sets feelingEditing = true to reopen the prompt.
units.entry: Rendered from feelingSection; onTap user tap.

units.does: Persists rating + note on a detached task via persistFeeling; on success sets refreshedSession, exits edit mode and bumps the archive-change signal.

branches.effect: true: refresh + feelingEditing=false + notify; false (not in archive or write failed): return, prompt stays open with no error shown

flags.text: A failed or not-found save leaves the prompt open with no message; the user is not told the rating wasn't stored.

units.does: Read-modify-write of the archived session setting workoutMetadata.workoutFeeling and workoutFeelingNote (no-op on sessions without workoutMetadata); returns the stored session, nil when not found or on error (logged).

branches.effect: error logged at warning and nil returned

flags.text: When the archived session has no workoutMetadata, the optional-chained assignments are no-ops but updateArchived still rewrites the file and returns a non-nil session, so saveWorkoutFeeling exits edit mode as if saved while nothing was stored (contradicts the comment at line 61-62 that the UI never claims a save that didn't happen).

units.does: If the stored analysisSnapshot is missing or needsRebuild (older schema or different narrative language), builds a new WorkoutAnalysisSnapshot off-main from snapshotInputs and persists it.

branches.effect: true: needsRebuild decides; false: `??` true -> rebuild
false: return without work (current snapshot, or no samples/duration); true: build and persist

flags.text: The snapshot is built from `session` as it was when onAppear fired (usually initialSession, before reloadFromArchive lands) and then written into whatever is in the archive at persist time without checking it changed; a retrim/re-analyze that lands during the build gets a snapshot computed from the old samples stamped with the current schema/language, so needsRebuild never triggers a rebuild for it.

units.does: Builds WorkoutAnalysisSnapshotBuilder.Inputs from the session (sport, duration, distance, elevation, mean HR, samples, splits, TRIMP, decoupling) and the user's max HR/weight from UserSettingsBridge.snapshot(); nil without metadata, samples or duration.

branches.cond: workoutMetadata, non-empty samples and duration all present
branches.effect: false: nil (no backfill possible); true: inputs returned

flags.text: Max HR and weight come from UserSettingsBridge.snapshot(), which reads the global AppDependencies.current.app.settingsManager, not the SettingsManager injected into this view's environment (line 38), so a view hosted with an injected SettingsManager (tests/previews) builds the snapshot from different settings than it renders with.

units.does: Writes the snapshot into the archived session via updateArchived; on success sets refreshedSession, bumps the archive signal and logs; errors logged.

branches.effect: false (session not in archive): return silently; true: refresh + notify
error logged at warning, nothing else

flags.text: Unlike saveWorkoutFeeling (whose comment says the archive read-modify-write must run detached so the archiveLock never blocks main), this archive.update (full decode + hash + write) runs synchronously on the main actor after the async build.

units.does: Computes generateSessionAnalysis() and renders the 'HOW YOU DID' card only when the text is non-empty.
Card body: header plus the narrative text in a rounded card background.
Sparkles icon + 'HOW YOU DID' caption header.
Returns the stored snapshot's howYouDidNarrative when non-empty, else the legacy on-the-fly narrative.

flags.text: The cached howYouDidNarrative is text frozen at build time with the units then in effect ('Climbed 300 m'), and needsRebuild only checks schema version and narrative language, so after the user switches metric/imperial the How-you-did card keeps the old unit while the key-stats ELEV GAIN tile shows the new one.

units.does: Joins up to five sentences (α1 regime, decoupling, HRR, TRIMP, elevation), skipping nil ones; '' when duration < 1 min.

flags.text: Legacy narrative (alpha1RegimeSentence/regimeWording, decouplingSentence, trimpSentence, elevationSentence, hrrSentence) re-implements WorkoutAnalysisSnapshotBuilder.buildHowYouDidNarrative with diverging rules: the builder guards 'the full N min' with a 90% coverage check, words TRIMP as 'Training load' with no <30 cutoff, and has no HRR sentence; the legacy one says 'TRIMP N', drops <30, and adds HRR. The same workout reads differently before and after its snapshot backfill.

units.does: α1 regime sentence from band seconds (shared Alpha1ReportCards totals); nil when no α1 or zero banded time.
Words the session shape from easy/threshold/hard seconds (converted to minutes).

branches.effect: 'Solid aerobic-base effort — α1 stayed above threshold for the full <totalMin> min.'

flags.text: The all-easy sentence claims α1 stayed above threshold 'for the full <totalMin> min' using total session duration, even when α1 readings covered only part of the session (banded seconds are ignored here).

units.does: Pa:Hr decoupling sentence for sessions ≥10 min: <5% strong efficiency, <8% mild drift, else significant loss.

branches.effect: 'stayed at … strong aerobic efficiency' (also for any negative value)

units.does: Lucia TRIMP sentence with fixed bands: ≥150 heavy, ≥80 moderate, ≥30 light, otherwise nil.
'You climbed X.' when elevation gain ≥ 30 m, formatted in the user's units.

Shapes WorkoutHeroCard inputs: sport (default walk), formatted distance or '—', duration label, pace label, end date, dominant α1 band, snapshot hero narrative or legacy heroNarrative, route coordinates from the decoded track.

branches.effect: used verbatim (snapshot init stores empty as nil); else `??` legacy heroNarrative

flags.text: Comments say subsequent opens are 'pure field reads — no per-render iteration over thousands of samples' and 'One field read, no sample iteration', but heroCard calls heroDominantAlpha1Band on every body pass, which runs ectopicShadows plus a full α1 walk over all samples even when the snapshot already stores dominantAlpha1BandRaw.

units.does: Formats session.duration as H:MM:SS or M:SS; '—' with no end date.
Pace label for distance > 100 m and duration > 10 s via UnitsPreference.formatPace(elapsedSec:distanceMeters:); nil otherwise.

branches.effect: false: nil; true: formatted pace (elapsed, not moving, time)

units.does: 'Recover / fix this workout' block: RecoverSessionFromStrapButton, RecoveredRouteFromWatchButton and the retrim control.
RecoveredWorkoutTrimControl whose action awaits collector.retrimRecoveredWorkout(sessionId:endSec:); identity keyed on session.endDate so it resets after a trim.
units.entry: Rendered from recoverWorkoutSection; trim closure on user action.

units.does: Orange banner: warning icon, reason.displayLabel, and the explainer text including recoveredAt.
ViewModifier body: 10% orange rounded fill with 35% orange 1pt border.
Explainer copy per PartialDataReason; appCrashed appends the recovery time when known.
WorkoutKeyStatsCard over keyStatTiles.
Assembles tiles in order: HR tiles, elevation, primary load, secondary HRSS, best split.

flags.text: USERS_MANUAL says the headline stats show distance, duration, avg pace, top speed, elevation gain, HR avg/peak, cadence, power, METs, calories, TRIMP and HRSS. The key-stats card builds only AVG HR, PEAK HR, ELEV GAIN, one LOAD/TRIMP tile, HRSS (only when powerTSS is stored) and BEST SPLIT; top speed, cadence, power, METs and calories are not tiles.

units.does: Appends AVG HR (session.meanHR, truncated) and PEAK HR (max sample heartRate) tiles when present.
Appends ELEV GAIN tile when gain > 2 m.
Appends the primary LOAD/TRIMP tile from preferredTrainingLoad (rounded value, source-specific subtitle, bolt icon/yellow for power else waveform/dusty rose).
Subtitle: route-history extrapolation estimate when it exceeds the recorded load by >1 (named route at confidence ≥0.55), otherwise a per-source caption marking partial data.

branches.cond: extrapolatedTRIMP and confidence present and est > load+1

branches.effect: '~N est · <route>' else '~N est for full route'

flags.text: extrapolatedTRIMP (a Lucia-TRIMP-scale route estimate) is compared with load.value whatever its source (power TSS, HRSS or METs load), and with any confidence, so a power or HRSS workout whose route estimate exceeds its TSS by more than 1 gets the subtitle '~N est for full route' under the LOAD tile. The comment calls this the strap-dropped case, but it does not use routeEstimateReplacesHRLoad, so it also fires on normal easier runs of the route.

units.does: Tile label: LOAD for power/hr/mets, TRIMP for banister/routeHistory.
Appends an HRSS tile (hrTSS) when stored powerTSS is non-nil.

flags.text: Gate checks the raw stored powerTSS, but the primary tile uses computedPowerTSS (>0, derived from NP+FTP when not stored): a stored powerTSS of 0 makes hrTSS the primary LOAD and shows the same number again as HRSS, and a read-time-derived power load gets no HRSS comparison tile — contrary to the comment 'only when the power-based load is the primary'.

units.does: Appends BEST SPLIT tile from bestSplitDisplay (pace + caption) when available.

flags.text: The BEST SPLIT tile reads WorkoutStatsCards.bestSplitDisplay, which uses the raw stored splits (not the unit-resolved cachedSplits the splits card renders) and picks the unit label per split (distance > 1500 m). So a partial final split can win as fastest and be labelled 'km' on a mile-bucketed workout, and km-stored splits show as 'km N' for an imperial user whose splits card lists miles. Share.swift:487-490 describes this exact per-row mislabel.

units.does: Sums seconds per LiveDFAAnalyzer display band over artifact-filtered α1 readings and returns the band with most time; nil when none.

branches.cond: a max band exists with > 0 s
branches.effect: false: nil; true: that band (ties resolve by dictionary order)

flags.text: Re-derives the dominant α1 band that the snapshot stores as dominantAlpha1BandRaw, with different rules: the builder collapses the hard bands and breaks ties below>between>above, this uses LiveDFAAnalyzer.Band.display bands and Dictionary.max, whose tie result depends on hash order.

units.does: Lists α1 readings with their timed seconds (gap since previous α1 sample capped by Alpha1ReportCards.sampleSeconds), excluding those inside ectopic shadows.
Legacy hero narrative: '' for <1 min; 'α1 not captured' without α1; all-easy / all-hard sentences; crossing narrative when a sustained AT1 crossing exists; else minute breakdown.

flags.text: Unlike the builder's hero narrative (guard below+btwn+above > 0), this only checks that some sample has alpha1; when every α1 reading falls in an ectopic shadow, alpha1BandTotals returns all zeros and the line 569 branch claims 'α1 stayed above threshold the whole time. Ideal Zone-2 session.' with zero measured α1 time.

heroNarrative/crossingNarrative duplicate WorkoutAnalysisSnapshotBuilder.buildHeroNarrative/crossingNarrative with different wording and without its coversSession guard; the legacy text shows only until the snapshot backfill lands.

units.does: Delegates to Alpha1ReportCards.alpha1BandTotals with ectopic shadows from the same samples.
'Crossed aerobic threshold at m:ss [at N bpm]' plus hard minutes (mixed) or threshold/easy minutes.

260pt placeholder with spinner and 'Loading route…'.
